proposals.before: Dividing the dividend by the divisor yields winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight—one day later than the Yuankai Calendar, which matches the true count of celestial days.
proposals.after: Dividing the dividend by the divisor yields winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight—one day later than the Yuanjia Calendar, which matches the true count of celestial days.
proposals.reason: 元嘉曆 is Yuanjia, not Yuankai; the packet English misspells the calendar name.

proposals.before: Divide the dividend by the divisor; one obtains winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight, one day later than the Yuankai Calendar—the correct reckoning of heaven's days.
proposals.after: Divide the dividend by the divisor; one obtains winter solstice's added hour at thirty-one ke after midnight, one day later than the Yuanjia Calendar—the correct reckoning of heaven's days.
proposals.reason: 元嘉曆 is Yuanjia; literal English incorrectly has Yuankai.

proposals.before: In the third year of the Xiaping era of Later Han, the Monograph on the Quarter-remainder Calendar records the mid-term shadow at Start of Winter as 1 zhang and at Beginning of Spring as 9 chi 6 cun.
proposals.after: In the third year of the Xiping era of Later Han, the Monograph on the Quarter-remainder Calendar records the mid-term shadow at Start of Winter as 1 zhang and at Beginning of Spring as 9 chi 6 cun.
proposals.reason: 熹平 is Xiping in standard pinyin; Xiaping is a misspelling (cf. s0205 Xiping).

proposals.before: In Xiaping year 3, the calendar then in use fixed the winter solstice on dingchou, with the added hour exactly at midday.
proposals.after: In Xiping year 3, the calendar then in use fixed the winter solstice on dingchou, with the added hour exactly at midday.
proposals.reason: 熹平 should be Xiping, matching the corrected form used later in the chapter.

proposals.before: Measured with the new table: 9 chi 6 cun 7 fen and a half; Wang Pu's calculation: 1 zhang 1 chi 5 fen; new method: 1 zhang 6 cun 8 fen 7 small fen.
proposals.after: Measured with the new table: 9 chi 6 cun 7 fen and a half; Wang Pu's calculation: 1 zhang 1 cun 5 fen; new method: 1 zhang 6 cun 8 fen 7 small fen.
proposals.reason: Chinese 一丈一寸五分 is 1 zhang 1 cun 5 fen; idiomatic invents an extra chi.

proposals.before: New table measured shadow length 9 chi 6 cun 7 fen half; Wang Pu calculated shadow length 1 zhang 1 chi 5 fen; new method calculated shadow length 1 zhang 6 cun 8 fen small fen 7.
proposals.after: New table measured shadow length 9 chi 6 cun 7 fen half; Wang Pu calculated shadow length 1 zhang 1 cun 5 fen; new method calculated shadow length 1 zhang 6 cun 8 fen small fen 7.
proposals.reason: Chinese 一丈一寸五分 lacks 尺; literal wrongly inserts chi.

decisions.reason: Source 《元嘉曆》 is the Yuanjia Calendar (元嘉); Yuankai misreads 嘉 as kai, and the proposed Yuanjia restores the correct calendar name without other changes.
The same 《元嘉曆》 must be Yuanjia in the literal field; Yuankai is a pinyin error, and the replacement corrects only that name.
Source 熹平三年 uses the era 熹平, standard pinyin Xiping; Xiaping invents an incorrect first syllable, and the proposed form matches the Chinese era name.
Unit 熹平三年 again names the Xiping era; idiomatic Xiaping is the same misspelling, and Xiping is the accurate repair.
王朴算景長一丈一寸五分 is 1 zhang 1 cun 5 fen with no 尺; idiomatic “1 zhang 1 chi 5 fen” invents a chi, and “1 zhang 1 cun 5 fen” restores the Chinese measures.
The same 一丈一寸五分 lacks 尺; literal “1 zhang 1 chi 5 fen” wrongly inserts chi, and “1 zhang 1 cun 5 fen” is the accurate reading.
